23/S0.subgoal: Explain the motivation for treating XR systems as interactive systems and describe the disappearing-technology ideal, relating it to presence and historical computing trends.

23/S1.subgoal: Explain that interactive systems involve lay users and why designers should avoid forcing users to learn the underlying technology.

23/S2.subgoal: Describe the user-centric approach to designing interactive systems.

23/S3.subgoal: Define human-computer interaction and identify its core concern as incorporating humans into design.

23/S4.subgoal: Explain why human factors require knowing user characteristics, using a railway ticket-booking example to show that different users need different interfaces.

23/S5.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture and preview the next part.
